- Request shapes: Primary experience is chat (interactive streaming preferred). We also will bulk-generate summaries nightly using non-stream batch completions. 

- Tokenization & length: Typical user message ~80–180 tokens; we usually send a system prompt + 4–5 prior turns; total context sits around 1,000–1,500 tokens. For generation we want a soft cap near 256 tokens and enforcement of explicit stop tokens ("###END") for structured outputs.

- Reranker/embeddings: We'll feed embeddings from nightly ingestion; expected indexing QPS small (batch daily), but query QPS could be 100–200 at peak, top-K rerank of 25–50 looks right for relevance. We also want semantic freshness within 24 hours for new content.

I'll link a small sample of anonymized chat logs to the Drive link later today.

Hi Aisha — hi Rishi, quick technical notes based on Aisha's answers:

1) Auth: For the PoC, a scoped API key is easiest (rotateable, time-limited). If you want OAuth later, Redwood supports provider-based OAuth and token exchange flows for private deployments. For the scoped key we can provide short-lived tokens with IP restrictions.

2) Streaming vs completions: you're best off using streaming chat for the interactive assistant to achieve fast first-byte latency. Implementation notes: 
- Redwood streaming uses SSE (server-sent events) or websocket streams depending on SDK; the server emits "delta" chunks (tokens or token-groups).
- Client should render first_token immediately and append subsequent deltas. We support an optional "final_chunk" marker to indicate completion.
- For stop tokens: include a list of string stops in the request (e.g., ["###END"]). Redwood will attempt to stop generation on the token boundary; you should still enforce a client-side guard in case of non-exact matches.

3) Tokenization & max_tokens: Given ~1k–1.5k context and desired gen cap 256, set max_tokens=256 and also set model_max_total_tokens to slightly above expected context + generation to avoid rejections. If using streaming with prefix caching, small increases to context won't recompile kernels in most cases.

4) Structured output / tool-calling: We recommend a JSON-schema-first approach: 
- Provide a lightweight JSON schema describing the output object (fields, types, enums).
- Use Redwood's tool-calling layer to map schema results to webhook calls. Example: 
  - When model emits {"action":"create_ticket","ticket":{"summary":"..."}}, Redwood can POST to your ticketing webhook with a transform.
- For safety, configure a validator stage that rejects outputs not matching the schema and returns an "invalid_schema" reason to the client.

5) Embeddings & reranker: For nightly ingestion + top-50 rerank: use a hybrid candidate retrieval (approx NN index) + rerank pass using a cross-encoder where latency allows. Redis or vector DB for ANN is fine; Redwood integrates via pull connectors or we can host a dedicated ANN layer if you want co-located latency.

I'll drop a short example request/response pair and a JSON schema to the Drive link.

Ben

Aisha — adding a couple architectural constraints and an ask for the PoC kickoff: 

- Routing & model selection: we'll propose a policy that routes interactive chat to a low-latency Llama-variant (quantized) and falls back to a higher-capacity LLM for heavy-generation tasks. This keeps cost predictable and provides graceful degradation.
- KV/prefix caching: enable prefix caching for repeated system prompts and short lived session caching for conversational state to meet the 250ms first-token target.
- Tool calling: For PoC, we'll map two tool hooks: (1) ticket.create -> POST to your /webhooks/ticket endpoint, (2) knowledge.search -> internal reranker call. We'll include a validation lambda to guard outputs.
- Embeddings: recommend top-K=40 for initial tuning; if latency budget allows, bump to 50. We'll run an offline eval against your sample set.

Ask before kickoff: please upload an anonymized sample of 200–500 chat turns (JSONL) and a small set of knowledge docs (5–10 items) so we can pre-compute embeddings and tune reranker thresholds. Drop to the Drive link or reply with a secure file share.

Link: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2bSynTech-ReqRespDoc (added example schema and example request/response)

Laura
